subject: Pilot governance checkpoints and evidence journal
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Nambiar <asha@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot governance checkpoints and evidence journal

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our discussion, I sketched a compact governance plan so your team can validate risk, performance, and integration before committing to Dedicated. Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an "evidence journal" template that maps each exit gate to the artifacts we expect to collect (logs, smoke-test outputs, KPI dashboards).

High-level proposal (2-week pilot):
- Week 0: Environment prep + baseline data ingest (infra checklist + test corpus)
- Week 1: Functionality smoke tests + integration verification (API auth flows, KV cache sanity)
- Week 2: Performance sampling + qualitative evals (latency SLO sampling, hallucination spot-checks)

Exit gates we want to validate for pilot close:
1) Connectivity & security: successful end-to-end calls from your infra to our VPC connector, evidence: connection log + auth audit
2) Data handling: no PII leak in outputs, evidence: sampled transcripts + redaction checklist
3) Latency & stability: p50/p95 under target for key routes, evidence: token-level trace outputs + per-route latency dashboard export
4) Quality & safety: pass concordance thresholds on the 100-case prompt set, evidence: eval summary + spot-check notes

Can you confirm this cadence and whether Mark should be looped in on the technical checklist? If this looks good I’ll drop a cleaned MAP and the acceptance-evidence template into the shared Drive and propose kickoff times.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Nambiar <asha@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Dobson <mark.dobson@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot governance checkpoints and evidence journal

Sean —

This looks like the right level of detail, thank you. Two quick notes from our side:
- We need a slightly longer data-handling window to run our de-identification pipeline (adds 2 business days)
- For quality checks, our clinical reviewers want a separate "safety adjudication" step for any flagged hallucinations, with a template for notes so we can audit decisions later

Mark will take point on the connection test and will be available for a 30-minute run-through tomorrow afternoon. Please add him to the Drive folder.

Also: can you add an explicit rollback trigger in the MAP in case our telemetry shows a run of errors > 3% for more than 15 minutes? That was a hard requirement from InfoSec.

Best,
Asha
Asha Nambiar
Head of Data Platform, ClearPath Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot governance checkpoints and evidence journal

Forwarding Asha's note — agree we should bake in the de-id window and a clear rollback trigger. Ben, can you draft the explicit telemetry threshold language and a compact remediation play (who disables the route, who notifies the customer, SLAs for investigation)? I'll take ownership of the safety adjudication template with a clinical reviewer-friendly layout.

On the attachments: I'll update the MAP to include a column for the required artifact type (dashboard CSV export, anonymized transcript, adjudicator notes) so handoff to ClearPath's audit team is straightforward.

Onboarding checklist items to add:
- Drive folder with subfolders: evidence/raw-logs, evidence/summaries, evidence/adjudication
- Doc: runbook for rollback steps with primary and secondary contacts

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot governance checkpoints and evidence journal

On Tue, May 16, 2027 at 11:25 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Asha's note — agree we should bake in the de-id window and a clear rollback trigger. Ben, can you draft the explicit telemetry threshold language and a compact remediation play (who disables the route, who notifies the customer, SLAs for investigation)? I'll take ownership of the safety adjudication template with a clinical reviewer-friendly layout.

Thanks — draft below for MAP column text and rollback trigger (feel free to redline):
- Telemetry trigger: error-rate > 3% sustained for 15m on the production route OR any single 1-minute spike to 7%+ error rate
- Immediate action: automated route disable (failover to smaller-capacity safe-instance), page Redwood SRE and ClearPath on-call, mark pilot "paused" in MAP
- Incident window: 2 hours for hot-fix or rollback; if unresolved, schedule a leadership review within 24 hours

I'll also add a short checklist for test harness runs (auth token validity, KV cache warm, baseline sampling points) so the first integration day is reproducible. Attaching the acceptance-evidence-template.pdf with example exports.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acceptance-evidence-template.pdf

From: Mark Dobson <mark.dobson@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Asha Nambiar <asha@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot governance checkpoints and evidence journal

Folks —

Great work pulling this together. Quick confirmation from our engineering lead: the Drive layout and the trial cadence look fine, we’ll expect the 2-business-day de-id as a gating item before any qualitative review happens. Two asks from our side before kickoff:
1) Can Redwood provide a small sample export from a previous non-sensitive pilot that demonstrates the CSV layout you expect for the latency dashboard? We want to pre-wire our ingestion scripts.
2) Please include an explicit acceptance test for token-scoped rate-limiting — we want to ensure our downstream orchestration will handle burst traffic rather than rate-limit silently (evidence: token-level trace showing backpressure handling).

Lauren — copying you to confirm the commercial close path once the MAP is satisfied. What does success look like to us on Redwood's side to trigger the final purchase order?

Thanks,
Mark
Mark Dobson
Engineering Director, ClearPath Health

On Mon, May 17, 2027 at 10:00 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Sean/Marissa — happy to take point on the commercial close once ClearPath confirms the MAP. For our internal success criteria I propose: (a) pilot passes all 4 exit gates documented in the MAP; (b) no open high-severity items older than 48 hours at pilot close; (c) a signed mutual acceptance note in the Drive folder. I can prepare a short PO checklist and cover email to speed the final step.
>
>Lauren Bishop
>Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
